objective: Provide a linearizable takeover-vs-submission boundary and restore automatic eligibility after a successfully durable manager handoff, with no token-unaware coordinator send path.
required_changes: Replace check-only takeover intent with a synchronization primitive that atomically orders revoke against an actual G3 submission claim. If revoke wins, no frame/API submission occurs. If submission claim wins, classify the request as already in-flight/unknown and never claim cancellation or replay; takeover invocation must still record intent immediately without waiting for ACK/network completion.

Extend the combined lifecycle+Pause authority contract and G3BridgeServer final boundary minimally so the claim occurs immediately at the socket submission boundary, not merely before bridge.request. Retain existing plain authority-token compatibility and exact peer/run checks; malformed/throwing/non-boolean claims fail closed.

Remove or make impossible the token-unaware generic CommandPort fallback. Production and test command ports must implement the same bound authority contract; do not advertise invocation-time safety over one-shot check-only send.

In handoff, clear/reopen takeover intent only after external control returns a valid manager/control_wait state and that state is durably committed. If external handoff or durable commit fails, remain fail-closed. Confirm/takeover failure does not clear it.

Add deterministic tests for both total orders at the final check-to-_send_until boundary: revoke-before-claim gives zero frame; claim-before-revoke is already in-flight and preserves unknown/delivery evidence with no replay. Add same-coordinator takeover→confirm→handoff→automatic command/tick resumption and failed-handoff remains fenced.
